final_answer: Accept all 13 decision atoms to build OKO's empty-scene collection plus a self-correcting nightly retraining pipeline — 12 atoms as proposed and atom_13 (Gemini labeling) in modified form with label-quality safeguards. No atom is rejected outright; the judge returned 12 accepts and 1 modify, and the conflict matrix found no conflicts (micro-debate skipped). Two strong atoms anchor safety: the dry-run / auto_promote=FALSE default (atom_09, top score 0.92) and the verified-and-re-fixed FinetuneGate (atom_10) — together they guarantee no worse model is ever promoted unattended. Two bundled atoms (atom_06 nightly orchestrator, atom_08 GPU guard) are accepted in intent but DECOMPOSED into per-phase / per-component files+tests to honor the atomic-development principle (atom_12), matching the judge's scope penalties. Storage vs. dataset representation is reconciled: atom_02 keeps class_name='background' as storage metadata ONLY, while atom_03 is authoritative for the YOLO layer — negatives are images with EMPTY label files, never a synthetic 'background' object class. atom_13 is modified to add a confidence threshold, abstention/agreement handling, human spot-check sampling, and a hard rule that the held-out eval set (atom_10) is NOT Gemini-labeled, so VLM noise cannot poison the gate. Build order is safety-first: prove the gate correct BEFORE any auto-promotion path exists, ship the data-collection feature (the genuinely new component) in parallel, and keep promotion human-gated via Telegram until the operator confirms a dry-run night.

decisions.decision: atom_01 — Extend CropCollector with an EmptySceneSampler, multi-triggered by a configurable timer, a no-detection frame threshold, and the scene-memory background-only signal, to collect true-negative/background frames.
decisions.rationale: Tri-proposal consensus (A,B,C), judge total 0.805. Collecting background frames is standard CV practice and the direct upstream lever against false positives; the user explicitly asked to periodically capture and label empty scenes. Implemented as an extension of the existing CropCollector, so feasibility is high.
alternatives_considered: Single-trigger (timer only) sampling — rejected as too brittle / misses event-driven gaps
No empty-scene collection — leaves the model prone to hallucinating presence on background
decisions.risk: Collection alone yields only indirect risk reduction; over-collection could flood the dataset with near-identical empty frames. Mitigated by the balancer (atom_05) and frame_hash dedup (atom_02).
decisions.test: `pytest oko` verifies EmptySceneSampler collects frames under each trigger (timer, no-detection threshold, scene-memory background_only) and not when a person/animal is detected.

decisions.decision: atom_02 — Store empty/background examples in runs/labels/<cam>/ with explicit metadata: sample_type=empty_negative, class_name=background|empty, timestamp, camera_id, frame_hash, trigger_reason, and a source-detections snapshot.
decisions.rationale: Single-proposal (A) but complementary, judge total 0.8125. Rich, specific metadata gives strong traceability and is cheap. frame_hash enables dedup; trigger_reason and the detections snapshot make every sample auditable.
alternatives_considered: Minimal metadata (path + timestamp only) — rejected, loses provenance/auditability
Treating class_name as a dataset label — rejected, see reconciliation with atom_03
decisions.risk: class_name='background' could leak into the YOLO label layer and create a spurious object class. Mitigated by making atom_03 authoritative: class_name here is STORAGE metadata only.
decisions.test: `pytest oko` verifies empty/background samples are written with the full metadata schema and correct file structure under runs/labels/<cam>/.

decisions.decision: atom_03 — Represent empty scenes in the YOLO export as background images with EMPTY label files (true negatives); never emit a 'background' object box. Preserve nc/names back-compatibility.
decisions.rationale: Single-proposal (B), highest judge total in the data layer (0.875). This is the correct YOLO convention and actively prevents a common, model-degrading mistake (synthetic background class). It is the authoritative dataset representation that atom_02's storage metadata defers to.
alternatives_considered: Adding a 'background' object class with boxes — rejected (degrades detector, breaks nc/names)
Dropping empty frames at export — rejected, defeats the purpose of negative mining
decisions.risk: Low. Must keep the export reconciled with atom_02 storage metadata so background-tagged storage maps to empty-label-file output.
decisions.test: `pytest oko` verifies DatasetExporter produces image+empty-label-file pairs for negative samples and does not introduce a background class into names.

decisions.decision: atom_04 — Store hard-negatives as a separate sample_type=hard_negative, sourced from false positives, rejected detections, and Gemini-relabeled background/other where the live model fired person/animal.
decisions.rationale: Single-proposal (A), judge total 0.7975. Hard-negative mining is the most direct lever on precision and is cleanly separated by its own sample_type so the balancer can ratio it independently.
alternatives_considered: Folding hard-negatives into generic empty_negatives — rejected, loses the high-value FP signal and balancing control
No hard-negative capture — rejected, leaves precision regressions uncorrected
decisions.risk: Moderate feasibility: requires plumbing FP-capture and relabel signals from several sources (live inference, gate rejections, Gemini disagreement). Build incrementally.
decisions.test: `pytest oko` verifies hard-negative samples are stored with sample_type=hard_negative and correct source-tracking provenance.

decisions.decision: atom_05 — Add an explicit, policy-driven dataset balancer to DatasetExporter (configurable max_empty_ratio, max_hard_negative_ratio, min_positive_count or ratios such as 3:1:1) with deterministic seeded sampling and a logged manifest of counts.
decisions.rationale: Consensus (A,B), judge total 0.835. Class imbalance materially affects training; deterministic seeding makes runs reproducible and the manifest makes them auditable.
alternatives_considered: Unbalanced 'use everything' export — rejected (imbalance skews training)
Hard-coded ratio — rejected in favor of a configurable policy
decisions.risk: Placeholder ratios (3:1:1) need tuning against the real collected distribution; wrong ratios could starve positives or over-weight negatives. The logged manifest surfaces this each run.
decisions.test: `pytest oko` verifies the balancer applies the policy correctly (ratios, min counts), is deterministic under a fixed seed, and writes the count manifest.

decisions.decision: atom_06 (DECOMPOSED) — Build the nightly pipeline as a NightlyTrainingScheduler whose phases are implemented as SEPARATE files+tests (one per atom_12), not a monolith: discover due days → acquire lock → snapshot samples → Gemini labeling → export YOLO → train candidate → evaluate current-vs-candidate → gate verdict → notify → release lock. Triggered by an external scheduler within the 01:00–06:00 window.
decisions.rationale: Tri-proposal consensus (A,B,C), judge total 0.7775 with a 0.05 scope penalty for bundling ~10 phases. The phased design and fixed night window are sound; the decomposition resolves the tension with the atomic-development principle.
alternatives_considered: One monolithic scheduler object — rejected (violates atom_12, untestable in units)
Internal long-running daemon instead of external scheduler trigger — deferred to open question on scheduler mechanism
decisions.risk: Highest implementation cost / lowest simplicity; it coordinates many components. Per-phase files+tests and the run ledger (atom_07) keep each piece shippable and recoverable.
decisions.test: `pytest oko` verifies phases execute in order, acquire/release the lock, produce the expected artifacts, and can be driven via a CLI entrypoint.

decisions.decision: atom_07 — Implement idempotency + catch-up via a run ledger / per-date marker directories with terminal STATUS files (PENDING, TRAINED, PROMOTED, ROLLED_BACK, DRYRUN), tracking date, input manifest hash, phase status, artifacts, verdict, and the dry_run flag; allow missed nights to be processed.
decisions.rationale: Consensus (A,B), judge total 0.8175. The correct idempotency pattern for an unattended nightly job — prevents duplicate/partial runs and enables safe resume after a crash.
alternatives_considered: No state tracking / fire-and-forget — rejected (duplicate or lost runs)
DB-backed state — rejected as overkill vs. file markers for a single-host job
decisions.risk: State-machine adds modest complexity; a stale lock from a crashed run must be reclaimable (tie to the watchdog, atom_08c).
decisions.test: `pytest oko` verifies marker/ledger files track status and manifest hash correctly and that a missed/incomplete date is detected and either resumed or skipped idempotently.

decisions.decision: atom_08 (DECOMPOSED into 08a/08b/08c) — Guard the GPU during training: (08a) an inference lockfile; (08b) pause or degrade live inference into a clearly-timed degraded mode with a Telegram/status notification; (08c) a night-window watchdog that aborts and rolls back if the 01:00–06:00 window is exceeded. Each sub-component is its own file+test.
decisions.rationale: Consensus (A,B,C), judge total 0.74 with a 0.05 scope penalty for bundling. Protecting a live-inference GPU from training contention and timeboxing the window are important; the lockfile is trivial but the degraded-mode and watchdog are intricate and must be tested separately.
alternatives_considered: Single bundled resource-manager atom — rejected (violates atom_12)
Killing live inference entirely during training — kept as a degraded-mode option pending operator preference (open question)
decisions.risk: Highest concern alongside atom_06: degrading live inference cleanly and aborting/rolling back mid-train is error-prone. Build and test 08a→08b→08c in that order.
decisions.test: `pytest oko` verifies the GPU lock is acquired/released, live inference enters degraded/paused mode with a timeout + notification, and the watchdog aborts and triggers rollback when the window is exceeded.

decisions.decision: atom_09 — Default dry_run=true / training.auto_promote=FALSE: run a full train+compare cycle, send a Telegram notification with before/after metrics and the gate verdict, but PREVENT auto-promotion until explicit operator confirmation.
decisions.rationale: Consensus (A,B,C), strongest atom in the set (0.9175). Nearly free (a config flag + notification) and the single biggest safety lever — human-in-the-loop before any unattended promotion. Directly satisfies the mandated first-run dry-run contract.
alternatives_considered: Auto-promote from night one — rejected (unverified gate + no operator review)
Manual-only training forever — rejected, defeats the continuous-improvement goal once trust is established
decisions.risk: Low. Residual question is the criterion for flipping auto_promote to TRUE (see open questions); until then promotion stays human-gated.
decisions.test: `pytest oko` verifies that with dry_run=true / auto_promote=FALSE no model is promoted, and a Telegram notification with before/after metrics + verdict is emitted.

decisions.decision: atom_10 — Verify-by-code and re-fix FinetuneGate: evaluate candidate-vs-current on a held-out set using actual DETECTION outputs (results[0].boxes; top-confidence box cls → label string), and gate on person-precision AND accuracy with a configurable epsilon margin, REJECTING any candidate that regresses person-precision even if other metrics improve. Explicitly confirm the 99034ac5 fix is real.
decisions.rationale: Consensus (A,B,C), judge total 0.82. The gate is the core safety boundary of the unattended pipeline. The task flags this verification as ОБЯЗАТЕЛЬНО and cites the 'literary-slop' lesson: do not trust 'done' — prove by regression tests that the gate refuses a worse model.
alternatives_considered: Gating on classification probabilities — rejected (wrong signal; this was the original bug)
Gating on accuracy alone / aggregate improvement — rejected (would let a person-precision regression through)
Trusting the prior 'done' status without code-level verification — rejected per the literary-slop lesson
decisions.risk: High cost — a verify-and-re-fix of existing buggy logic. Regression tests make it tractable and are the gating prerequisite for any auto-promotion path.
decisions.test: `pytest oko` regression tests assert the gate reads detection outputs, maps cls→label names, gates on person-precision AND accuracy with epsilon, and rejects a synthetically-worse candidate while accepting a clearly-better one.

decisions.decision: atom_11 — Implement crash-safe atomic model promotion via os.replace()/pointer swap, preserving the previous model and writing a rollback marker; never overwrite the live model file in place.
decisions.rationale: Consensus (A,B), judge total 0.895. Atomic rename eliminates half-written/corrupt models going live and makes rollback trivial — low cost, high risk-reduction.
alternatives_considered: Direct file overwrite on promote — rejected (corruption window, no rollback)
Copy-then-delete — rejected (non-atomic, leaves a torn state)
decisions.risk: Low. Must ensure the pointer/symlink-or-current-file convention is consistent with how live inference loads the model.
decisions.test: `pytest oko` verifies promotion is atomic (rename/pointer swap), the previous model is preserved, a rollback marker is written, and rollback restores the prior model.

decisions.decision: atom_12 — Adopt the atomic-development principle: each component ≈ one file + one test, verified by `pytest oko`; this is the governing standard that atoms 06 and 08 are decomposed against, and Architect-Claude reviews each atom.
decisions.rationale: Consensus (A,C), judge total 0.7975. Improves testability and keeps atoms shippable. It is a process heuristic ('approximately'), so it guides work rather than delivering functionality directly.
alternatives_considered: Large multi-feature commits — rejected (unreviewable, untestable in units)
decisions.risk: Heuristic boundary; some phases legitimately span more than one file. Apply judgment, keep one test per shippable unit.
decisions.test: Codebase-structure review plus `pytest oko` coverage existing for each atom before it is considered done.

decisions.decision: atom_13 (MODIFIED) — Integrate Gemini-2.5-flash for automated nightly labeling → YOLO via DatasetExporter, WITH added label-quality controls: a confidence threshold, agreement/abstention handling, human spot-check sampling, and a hard rule that the held-out evaluation set used by the gate (atom_10) is NOT Gemini-labeled (use a trusted/human-labeled held-out).
decisions.rationale: Single-proposal (C), judge verdict 'modify', total 0.765 with a 0.03 penalty. Automated VLM labeling is the bottleneck-breaker that makes nightly training viable (and is already implied by atom_06's labeling phase), but the original statement treated VLM output as ground truth. Unmitigated, VLM noise poisons both the training set and — fatally — the gate's held-out set.
alternatives_considered: Trust Gemini labels as ground truth with no safeguards — rejected (label noise poisons dataset and gate)
Gemini-label the held-out eval set too — rejected (would make the gate compare against noisy targets)
Human-label everything — rejected (defeats the automation goal; reserve humans for spot-checks and held-out)
decisions.risk: VLM label noise; risk-reduction scored low because, unmitigated, it INTRODUCES risk. The threshold/abstention/spot-check controls and the non-Gemini held-out provenance are mandatory mitigations, not optional.
decisions.test: `pytest oko` verifies Gemini labeling emits correct YOLO format, applies the confidence threshold and abstention handling, samples for human spot-check, and that the gate's held-out set is sourced from a non-Gemini (trusted) provenance.

rejected.decision: Represent empty scenes as a synthetic 'background' object class with bounding boxes.
rejected.why: Violates YOLO convention; negatives must be images with empty label files. A background object class degrades the detector and breaks nc/names back-compatibility (per atom_03, which is authoritative over atom_02's storage metadata).

rejected.decision: Treat Gemini-2.5-flash labels as ground truth with no quality safeguards, including labeling the gate's held-out set.
rejected.why: VLM label noise poisons the training set and, worse, the held-out set the gate compares against — silently defeating the entire safety boundary. Requires confidence threshold, abstention/agreement handling, human spot-check, and a non-Gemini held-out (atom_13 modify).

rejected.decision: Implement the nightly pipeline as a single monolithic scheduler object.
rejected.why: Bundling ~10 phases into one unit violates the atomic-development principle (atom_12) and is untestable in units; decomposed into per-phase files+tests (atom_06 scope penalty).

rejected.decision: Bundle the GPU lockfile, degraded live-inference mode, and night-window watchdog into one component.
rejected.why: Each is a distinct, independently-testable concern; bundling violates atom_12. Split into 08a/08b/08c (atom_08 scope penalty).

rejected.decision: Gate model promotion on classification probabilities, or on accuracy alone / aggregate metric improvement.
rejected.why: Classification probs were the original 99034ac5 bug; the gate must read detection outputs. Accuracy-only (or aggregate) gating would let a person-precision regression through — the gate must reject ANY candidate that regresses person-precision (atom_10).

rejected.decision: Promote a new model by overwriting the live model file in place.
rejected.why: Creates a corruption window where a half-written model can go live and leaves no rollback path; use atomic os.replace/pointer swap with previous-model preservation and a rollback marker (atom_11).

rejected.decision: Auto-promote from the first night without operator review.
rejected.why: The gate is unverified at first run and the contract mandates a dry-run; default auto_promote=FALSE with Telegram before/after metrics until explicit operator confirmation (atom_09).

open_questions: Scheduler mechanism: use the existing bridge nightly mechanism or a dedicated Windows scheduled task to trigger the 01:00–06:00 window? Contract allows either; needs an operator/architect decision.
Source of the trusted, non-Gemini held-out evaluation set (human-labeled subset vs. a reserved trusted slice) — who/what provides ground truth, given Gemini labels are barred from the held-out set?
Concrete dataset balance policy values — 3:1:1 (positive:empty:hard-negative) is a placeholder; needs tuning against the real collected distribution once the manifest reports actual counts.
Gemini labeling thresholds: specific confidence cutoff, abstention rule, and spot-check sampling rate.
Empty-scene sampling cadence: final timer interval (5 vs 10 min) and/or no-detection frame threshold, pending observed live data volume.
GPU contention policy during training: fully pause live inference or run a degraded mode, and what degraded-mode latency/availability is acceptable to the operator (atom_08b).
Promotion-trust criterion: after how many successful dry-run nights (or which explicit operator action) does training.auto_promote flip from FALSE to TRUE?

steps: EmptySceneSampler as a CropCollector extension with timer / no-detection-threshold / scene-memory background-only triggers
Empty/background storage metadata schema (sample_type=empty_negative, class_name as storage-only, frame_hash, trigger_reason, detections snapshot)
Hard-negative capture (sample_type=hard_negative) from FPs / rejected detections / Gemini disagreement
YOLO export: negatives as images with empty label files (authoritative; reconcile with A's storage metadata)
Policy-driven balancer with deterministic seeded sampling + logged manifest
Gemini-2.5-flash labeling with confidence threshold / abstention / spot-check, held-out set kept non-Gemini

implementation_plan.phase: C — Safety core (build and prove BEFORE any auto-promote path)
steps: Verify-by-code + re-fix FinetuneGate: detection outputs, cls→label, person-precision AND accuracy with epsilon, reject regressions — write the regression tests first
Atomic model promotion via os.replace/pointer swap + previous-model preservation + rollback marker
NightlyTrainingScheduler phases as separate files+tests, CLI-triggerable in the 01:00–06:00 window
Run ledger / per-date markers with terminal STATUS files, manifest hash, idempotent catch-up
Degraded/paused live-inference mode with timeout + Telegram/status notification (08b)
Night-window watchdog that aborts + rolls back on overrun, reclaims stale locks (08c)
Default dry_run=true / auto_promote=FALSE: full train+compare cycle, Telegram before/after metrics + gate verdict, no promotion without operator confirmation
Run the first real night as a dry-run under operator review; flip auto_promote to TRUE only after explicit confirmation
Hold to one-file/one-test atoms verified by `pytest oko`; Architect-Claude reviews each atom before it is marked done

next_step: Start with atom_10: verify-by-code that the FinetuneGate fix (99034ac5) genuinely compares detection outputs (not classification probabilities), maps cls→label names, gates on person-precision AND accuracy, and promotes atomically — write the `pytest oko` regression tests that prove the gate REFUSES a synthetically-worse candidate. The gate is the safety boundary the entire unattended pipeline depends on, and per the literary-slop lesson its 'done' status must be proven by code before any auto-promotion path is built.

red_team_findings.what: Held-out ground truth is the current model's own output, making the gate circular. crop_collector.py:70,84 sets class_name = detection.class_name (the live model's prediction at capture time), and eval_harness.evaluate compares the candidate's predictions against that same field as 'truth'.
red_team_findings.why: A candidate scores 'better' by agreeing MORE with the current model's past detections — including its false positives. The gate measures self-agreement, not correctness, so it structurally rewards reproducing the current model (incl. its errors) and cannot validate real improvement. atom_13 (Gemini labels) is meant to replace this, but the decision never states the held-out ground truth must come from an INDEPENDENT/human source; open_questions lists held-out 'construction' but omits the label-source validity problem. If held-out is labeled by the same Gemini that labels training, the gate measures agreement-with-Gemini and a Gemini-trained candidate beats the current model almost by construction — defeating the gate's conservatism.

red_team_findings.what: 'FinetuneGate-коррекция done' (known_context) is false; the live gate is the explicitly-REJECTED design and is non-functional. finetune_gate.py:50 gates on accuracy ALONE with strict '>', no person-precision, no epsilon. _predict_all (:94-96) reads classification .probs.top1 and emits str(cls_id) (e.g. '3'), which evaluate compares against name labels (e.g. 'person') — they can never match, so accuracy is ALWAYS 0.0 for BOTH models, improved is ALWAYS False, and the gate NEVER promotes anything.
red_team_findings.why: The decision builds atoms 01-09 'on top of' a gate it characterizes as merely needing test-verification ('prove it's done'). In reality the gate (a) implements the rejected accuracy-only path, (b) has the exact cls-id-vs-label-name bug atom_10 names, and (c) for a detection model results[0].probs is None so every prediction is '__missing__'. Step 1 is a rewrite, not a verification — the project's true state is mis-stated, under-scoping the highest-risk work and invalidating the claim that the 5-stage foundation's safety core is complete.

red_team_findings.what: The existing pytest suite is a false green that proves nothing about the gate. test_finetune_gate.py:70-95 mocks the eval harness and asserts only that an 'improved' key exists and is a bool; no test checks person-precision gating, detection outputs, cls→name mapping, atomic promotion, or epsilon.
red_team_findings.why: success_tests 'all new components covered by passing pytest oko' and 'verified by pytest oko' are satisfiable while the gate is broken — exactly the 'literary-slop: don't trust done' failure the contract warns about, present in the foundation's own tests. Any claim of 'pytest oko green' as evidence the gate is safe is unfounded; the green suite co-exists with a gate that can never promote and never checks the safety metric.

red_team_findings.what: The gate omits recall, and this feature actively biases the model toward the failure recall would catch. atom_10 gates on person-precision AND accuracy only. The new empty/hard-negative collection (atoms 01-05) floods the dataset and held-out with negatives.
red_team_findings.why: A candidate that suppresses detections scores HIGH person-precision (few, confident TPs) and HIGH accuracy (held-out dominated by empties), so it passes the gate while missing real persons/intrusions — the dangerous direction for a security detector. The empty-collection feature structurally pushes toward this exact regime, and the gate is blind to it. Gating on precision+accuracy without recall/F1 lets a 'detect almost nothing' model win.

red_team_findings.what: atom_10 mandates detection-box evaluation, but the entire data/eval stack is crop-classification with no IoU matching. CropRecord stores a single cropped object + one class_name; eval_harness builds a single-label-per-item confusion matrix (eval_harness.py:96-108). True detection person-precision needs IoU-matched TP/FP against ground-truth boxes on full frames.
red_team_findings.why: The decision calls correct box handling 'fiddly (feasibility 0.7).' In fact it requires a NEW evaluation subsystem (IoU matching, multi-box GT) AND a NEW held-out representation (full frames with box annotations) that the foundation does not produce — the positives are crops. This is a major architectural gap mislabeled as a small fix, and it conflicts with the crop-based positives already being collected into runs/labels/<cam>/.

red_team_findings.what: Promotion is non-atomic in the live code, contradicting atom_11's 'os.replace/pointer-swap' claim. finetune_gate.py:82-83 does current_weights_link.unlink() then shutil.copy2(new, current) — a multi-second window where NO model exists at the active path. On win32 the intended os.replace also raises PermissionError if the live detector holds the .pt file handle.
red_team_findings.why: A crash or power loss mid-copy destroys the active model with no in-place fallback (the archive is a copy of the OLD weights, but the live link is already gone). The decision asserts atomicity as an existing property; it isn't. And the Windows-specific open-handle failure mode means even the planned os.replace needs the live inference process to release the model handle under the GPU lock — never specified in atom_08.

red_team_findings.what: The nightly trigger assumes the host is awake 01:00-06:00 — unverified and likely false on this machine. The scheduler mechanism is still an open_question; the host is a personal Windows desktop (OneDrive\Documents) that probably sleeps/hibernates overnight.
red_team_findings.why: Windows Task Scheduler will not run a sleeping/hibernating machine without explicit wake timers (and never wakes on battery/modern-standby). success_test 'triggers reliably within the ~01:00-06:00 window' then has no verified implementation. Catch-up (atom_07) masks the miss but pushes training into the DAY against the live detector — the GPU-contention scenario atom_08 was designed to avoid — turning a missed window into a daytime degradation.

red_team_findings.what: The held-out set is not actually frozen across nights, and the split leaks near-duplicates. eval_harness.freeze_held_out (:57-65) shuffles the full GROWING pool with fixed seed=42; because the pool length changes nightly, the held-out membership changes every run. The split is random with no temporal/camera dedup.
red_team_findings.why: The dry-run 'before/after' comparison and the gate's current-vs-candidate verdict are evaluated against a DIFFERENT held-out each night, so cross-night metrics and the operator's before/after report are not comparable. Random splitting (:58) puts near-identical consecutive frames in both train and held-out, inflating both models' metrics and letting an overfit candidate pass. open_questions flags held-out 'refresh' but not the leakage or the moving-target problem.

red_team_findings.what: Catch-up of missed nights conflicts with the timebox watchdog, and idempotency semantics are ambiguous. atom_07 catches up N missed dates 'exactly once' each; atom_08's watchdog aborts+rolls back if the 01:00-06:00 window is exceeded.
red_team_findings.why: Multiple sequential YOLO trainings on a single GPU cannot fit one ~5-hour window, so a backlog of missed nights causes every catch-up run to overrun and abort → permanent no-promote. No per-run time budget or 'train newest, defer rest' policy is specified. Separately, the manifest-hash + 'exactly once' rules conflict for late-arriving same-day samples: re-run because the hash changed, or skip because the date is terminal? Undefined.

red_team_findings.what: Readiness has no positive floor and the empty-frame storage collides with the crop-classification index. check_readiness (finetune_gate.py:18-24) counts all index.jsonl lines; atom_02 stores empties into runs/labels/<cam>/ with class_name=background.
red_team_findings.why: Once empties share index.jsonl, min_samples=100 can be met with ZERO positives, triggering training on a degenerate all-negative dataset. Empties are full FRAMES, but CropCollector/index.jsonl model single cropped objects with a class_name, and eval_harness.load_crops will treat 'background' as a classification label and try to classify whole frames. atom_02/03's storage choice is never reconciled with the existing crop-based readiness/eval path it must coexist with.

red_team_findings.what: The empty sampler is blind exactly where false positives occur. The 'no-detection' trigger (atom_01) only captures frames when there is NO detection, so it skips empty scenes in which the model hallucinates a detection — the FP-prone scenes that cause 'галлюцинации.'
red_team_findings.why: The sampler collects only 'easy' empties and never the hard empties that produce the false positives the feature is meant to correct. The hard-negative channel (atom_04) is the intended remedy but depends on reliably identifying FPs/Gemini-disagreements — itself unsolved (feasibility 0.75) and circular with the self-labeled data (finding 1). Net: the negative set may be rich in uninformative empties and poor in the corrective signal the goal requires.

red_team_findings.what: The pipeline hard-depends on Gemini availability/cost/rate-limits inside the night window with no fallback. atom_06 sequences labeling as a phase before export/train; a labeling failure aborts the run.
red_team_findings.why: Nightly full-day labeling has unbounded, unaddressed cost/quota, and a Gemini outage or rate-limit during 01:00-06:00 means no training that night — which then piles into catch-up (finding 9). No degraded path (label a sample, defer, retry) is specified, so an external API becomes a single point of failure for the whole self-correcting loop.

red_team_findings.what: The dry-run→promote handoff is undefined and Telegram is the only notify/confirm channel. The trained-but-withheld candidate's retention and one-action promotion after operator confirmation are unspecified; a terminal DRYRUN marker (atom_07) makes catch-up skip that date.
red_team_findings.why: After the operator reviews the before/after report and confirms, there is no defined way to promote THAT validated candidate — the DRYRUN-marked date is skipped on catch-up, so confirmation has nothing to act on without a fresh night, and the metrics the operator approved are stale. Telegram is also the sole delivery/confirmation path with no ack/retry/alternate; a delivery failure or no operator response silently stalls the loop in dry-run indefinitely.
